# Solution design assessment

## Evidence reviewed

- Full pinned story (source reference `user_story`, `characters 0-16000`; no further page): a local password-reset demonstration using Python 3.12, Flask, server-rendered pages, pytest, synthetic accounts and an in-memory notification sink; document production limitations; do not deploy or add deployment workflows.
- Supplied `sign-in-wireframe.png` (attachment source reference `941402b9-bfd8-414c-a6e4-2fc2dce190a1`, locator `sign-in-wireframe.png`): directly visible in the user's message as a white page with a centered thin outlined rectangular card, bold "Sign in" heading, "Email address" field with `name@example.com`, "Password" field with `********`, blue underlined "Forgot password?" link, wide dark "Sign in" button and "No account? Contact your administrator." footer. The attachment tool returned a reference, not image bytes; the image does not prove actual form behavior or link destination.
- Approved earlier outputs read by stage key: `requirements_analysis` (REQ-001 through REQ-024 and acceptance criteria), `ui_analysis` (observed versus proposed interactions), and `acceptance_20261025134159_ec2756_risk` (nine prospective risks, not observed defects). The stage-output tools returned no source-reference locator; do not invent one for contract citations.
- Curated account recovery standard (knowledge source reference `bcf198d8-a628-401c-8641-b726fcbd00b5`, locator `v1, chunk 0`): ACC-STD-01 requires a recovery link, identical public responses for existing/nonexisting accounts, and at most five reset requests per account per hour; ACC-STD-02 requires single-use links expiring 30 minutes after issuance and sign-out of all active sessions; ACC-STD-03 requires notification after every successful reset. Search returned five identically worded versions, not five distinct rules. No additional architecture or technology policy was returned.
- Repository currently contains SDLC predecessor documents and a synthetic-test README, but no application scaffold or test runner configuration. This assessment does not modify source files.

## Design implications for planning

All 24 approved requirements can be addressed by implementation tasks; no known requirement currently warrants a missing-coverage disposition. Plan small, dependency-ordered tasks covering Flask/Python setup and synthetic state; wireframe-faithful sign-in and active sessions; generic reset-request responses and known-account rolling-hour limiting; privately recorded reset links and single-use, issuance-based 30-minute validity; new-password submission, password change, all-session invalidation and owner notification; server-rendered accessible flow; pytest scenarios; and local setup/production-limitations documentation. The design must provide explicit route and state contracts, scoped access to the in-memory sink, security and reliability boundaries, and a dependency DAG. Deployment is out of scope: represent REQ-024 with a task verifying/documenting absence of deployment additions, not a deployment task.

Treat approved predecessor interpretations as design assumptions rather than quotations of the standard: email is the account identifier; five requests per account per hour means a rolling hour for known synthetic accounts, without inventing a quota for unknown identifiers; an unused link is valid before 30 minutes from issue and invalid at or after that boundary. The public response must not expose the account's existence, throttle status or recovery link. Only sign-in appearance is evidenced; reset-screen layout, exact text, password policy and authenticated success screen are not specified. Choose and label minimal local-demo presentation and testable behavior at design time, preserving the predecessor open questions; do not claim a production identity store, mail delivery, persistent session infrastructure or an implemented app.
